meta.title: Flipper Zero firmware fork analysis
meta.subtitle: NFC / SubGhz capability & provenance atlas
meta.note: Canonical source for both FEATURE-TREE.md and feature-explorer.html. Add features here and run the build.

forks.name: Official
forks.head: c9ab2b68
forks.summary: The canonical upstream. Conservative: region-locked TX, smaller key sets, no bundled external apps (distributed via App Hub). Every fork descends from its 2020 root commit 46d78a36.

forks.name: Unleashed
forks.head: 318bfc3b
forks.summary: Direct fork of official and the upstream of both RogueMaster and Momentum. Origin of nearly all added SubGhz/NFC capability: extra protocols, Keeloq learning, region-lock removal, EMV/ntag4xx, the largest MFC dictionary.

forks.name: RogueMaster
forks.head: ed963fd0
forks.summary: Tracks Unleashed via squashed content-sync (commit identity erased) and bundles the largest in-tree app pack (669 FAPs). Broadest attack surface; one original protocol (telcoma_edge).

forks.name: Momentum
forks.head: 8ed809fb
forks.summary: Continuation of Xtreme. Ingests Unleashed via real git merges (true ancestry) and tracks OFW directly. Integrates weather/TPMS/POCSAG into the core SubGhz lib; ships ProtoPirate; keeps the OTA region service.

items.label: Official base protocols
items.desc: The 52 upstream SubGhz protocol decoders/encoders (CAME, Nice, Princeton, Holtek…) inherited unchanged by every fork.
items.prov: Upstream OFW. Byte-identical core shared by all four.

items.label: aes_common
items.desc: Software AES-128 helper that AES-based remotes (e.g. Beninca ARC) call for decryption.
items.prov: U-origin (`db2dc8f64`, landed with beninca_arc). **R dropped it** — RogueMaster switched Beninca to the chip's hardware AES, so the SW helper is absent there.

items.label: allstar_firefly
items.desc: AllStar Firefly garage / gate remote, decode + encode capable.
items.prov: U-origin (`1f2022b87`, jlaughter). Propagated U→M by real merge (shared SHAs); U→R by squashed bulk import.

items.label: beninca_arc
items.desc: Beninca ARC AES rolling-code gate remote; implementation splits 3-ways across forks.
items.prov: U-origin (`db2dc8f64`, MX). **3-way md5 divergence**: U & M use software `aes_common`; R re-implemented it on hardware AES via `furi_hal_crypto` (`a2cf8be10`).

items.label: ditec_gol4
items.desc: DITEC GOL4 gate / barrier remote protocol.
items.prov: U-origin (`556a2dd3f`, MX).

items.label: elplast
items.desc: Elplast gate remote protocol.
items.prov: U-origin.

items.label: honeywell
items.desc: Honeywell wireless alarm door / window sensor decoder.
items.prov: U-origin.

items.label: jarolift
items.desc: Jarolift roller-shutter remote — Keeloq-family rolling code, transmit-capable.
items.prov: U-origin (`271c65a96`, MX). Consumes the Keeloq learning algorithms; full clone/TX.

items.label: keyfinder
items.desc: Key-finder beeper-tag protocol for locating lost tags.
items.prov: U-origin (`d18619ff5`, MX); U=R=M byte-identical.

items.label: nord_ice
items.desc: Nord / ICE remote protocol decoder.
items.prov: U-origin (`a5f47e3e6`, MX).

items.label: treadmill37
items.desc: Treadmill remote-control protocol.
items.prov: U-origin.

items.label: hormann_bisecur
items.desc: Hörmann BiSecur AES garage-door remote, transmit-capable.
items.prov: **R/M only** — the same upstream PR (user890104) landed in both; never in Unleashed. Momentum disables it in the registry (compiled but flash-gated).

items.label: telcoma_edge
items.desc: Telcoma Edge gate remote — RogueMaster's only original SubGhz protocol.
items.prov: **RogueMaster-exclusive & RM-original** (`529fdbad3`, Benjamin Tamasi). The only ground-up protocol authored in a fork rather than inherited.

items.label: x10
items.desc: X10 RF home-automation protocol, decode-only.
items.prov: **R-origin** (`889674048`, RogueMaster) → propagated to Momentum. Decode-only. M disables it in the registry.

items.label: Weather-station pack
items.desc: rtl_433-derived weather sensor decoders (Acurite, Oregon, LaCrosse, Auriol, Bresser…).
items.prov: **Momentum-only in the core lib**; ported from rtl_433 via the weather_station app (HTotoo `b9382c912`). RogueMaster ships the same set only as external FAP apps. Commented out of M's main registry → served by external apps.

items.label: TPMS pack
items.desc: Car tire-pressure sensor decoders; expose stable per-vehicle IDs (tracking vector).
items.prov: M-only core-lib (rtl_433 port, HTotoo). Passive RX. RogueMaster bundles the same as an external app.

items.label: POCSAG / pager pack
items.desc: POCSAG pager decoder that reconstructs pager message text content (intercept).
items.prov: M-only core-lib (Max Lapan `4c092c8e6`). RogueMaster bundles it as an external app.

items.label: tx_8300
items.desc: TX-8300 thermo / hygro weather sensor decoder.
items.prov: Momentum-only (core-lib).

items.label: star_line / kia / scher_khan
items.desc: Russian car-alarm decoders — present upstream, deleted from all three forks.
items.prov: **Deleted in all forks** via Unleashed `50b5ee103` "bipki removal" (MX, 2026-01-12) — "they are in other app". Were decode-only. Relocated to an external app (Momentum: ProtoPirate). A rare case of forks *removing* upstream capability.

items.label: Keeloq decode
items.desc: Decodes Keeloq hopping-code remotes used by gates, cars and alarms.
items.prov: Upstream.

items.label: Keeloq learning / derivation algos
items.desc: Five algorithms (Faac, AERF, Erreka, Pujol, decrypt-derived) to derive manufacturer keys and clone remotes.
items.prov: U-origin; `keeloq_common.c` is **md5-identical** across U/R/M (`c87b1211…`). The file grew 127→236 lines; `learning_pujol` added in U `63d49b6e4` (MX, 2026-04-21).

items.label: Keeloq manufacturer keystore
items.desc: AES-encrypted manufacturer-key store; forks roughly double the record count.
items.prov: Forks ship a larger keystore — **62 → 116 records** (U=R=M byte-identical, `c4d8342f…`). Crucially the file is **AES-encrypted at rest** (`Encryption: 1`); the key lives in the device secure enclave, **not** the repo. No plaintext keys are exposed; the `*_user.example` holds only `AABBCCDDEEFFAABB` placeholders.
evi: NO — key in enclave, not in repo

items.label: Keeloq emulate / clone / TX
items.desc: Transmit and replay captured Keeloq codes; forks add a Save flag.
items.prov: Send flag upstream; forks add Save flag.

items.label: Jarolift clone+TX
items.desc: Jarolift rolling-code clone and transmit, using Keeloq derivation.
items.prov: U-origin; full TX; consumes the Keeloq learning algos.

items.label: Hörmann BiSecur clone+TX
items.desc: BiSecur AES garage remote clone + transmit (Momentum ships it disabled).
items.prov: R/M only; full TX. Momentum registry-disables it.

items.label: Somfy / Nice / FAAC / Alutech: RX → TX
items.desc: Five decode-only garage/gate remotes upgraded to clone & transmit in the forks.
items.prov: Forks add `SubGhzProtocolFlag_Send` to faac_slh, somfy_keytis, somfy_telis, nice_flor_s and alutech_at_4n — turning five **decode-only** remotes into clone/emulate/TX-capable.

items.label: Security+ v1/v2 TX
items.desc: Chamberlain Security+ garage rolling-code transmit; forks add Save.
items.prov: Upstream TX; +Save flag in forks.

items.label: Mandatory region TX gate
items.desc: Geographic frequency lock that enforces legal transmit bands.
items.prov: **Unleashed guts it** to an always-allow stub. R/M keep the region service but add a user toggle `bypass_region` (default OFF).

items.label: Extended frequency range
items.desc: Widens TX/RX to the full CC1101 'YARD Stick' bands (281–361 / 378–481 / 749–962 MHz).
items.prov: All forks widen `is_frequency_valid`; opt-in toggle, default OFF via SD asset.

items.label: OTA region-provisioning service
items.desc: Service that provisions the region profile over-the-air at activation.
items.prov: U & R **delete** the region service; **Momentum keeps it** — the one fork retaining OTA region provisioning.

items.label: Unlock asset (SD, default OFF)
items.desc: SD-card file the user must add to enable the extended/dangerous range.
items.prov: All ship OFF; opt-in via SD card. U uses `dangerous_settings`; R/M use `extend_range.txt` (M generates it at runtime).

items.label: RX protocol-filter bypass
items.desc: Receives and decodes protocols that are otherwise blocked or disabled.
items.prov: RX-only `ignore_filter` added in all three forks; absent upstream.

items.label: External CC1101 extended range
items.desc: Extended-range logic mirrored for an external CC1101 radio module.
items.prov: Forks mirror the extended-range logic for the external radio path.

items.label: Bruteforce / BinRAW
items.desc: Brute-force gate codes and raw-bit replay tooling.
items.prov: The SubGHz Bruteforce app is not in the U firmware tree (lives in all-the-plugins); `bin_raw.c` is in the fork core libs.

items.label: Frequency analyzer hotkeys
items.desc: Detect a signal's frequency, then one-press jump straight to it.
items.prov: U adds OK-short → use-freq / OK-long → Read menu (`subghz_scene_frequency_analyzer.c:56-77`).

items.label: FSK 12 kHz modulation (FM12K)
items.desc: 12 kHz FSK deviation preset needed by certain remotes.
items.prov: M-added preset (`cc1101_configs.c:223`).

items.label: Subdriving (GPS geotag)
items.desc: Geotag captured signals via a UART GPS module (war-driving).
items.prov: RX-only UART NMEA; geotag stored locally. R `subghz_gps.c`, M `subghz_history.c:22-23`.

items.label: TX power setting
items.desc: Persisted, adjustable transmit power level.
items.prov: Momentum adds persisted TX power (`subghz_scene_radio_settings.c`).

items.label: Custom buttons
items.desc: Map the arrow keys to alternate remote button codes during replay.
items.prov: U-origin `lib/subghz/blocks/custom_btn.c`; supports Keeloq/Alutech/Nice/Somfy/Secplus2/CAME Atomo.

items.label: Timestamped save filename
items.desc: Auto-names saved captures by timestamp + protocol.
items.prov: U `subghz_scene_radio_settings.c:189-191`.

items.label: Official base set
items.desc: Twelve upstream NFC stacks (MIFARE Classic/DESFire/Plus/Ultralight, ISO14443 a/b 3/4, ISO15693, FeliCa, SLIX, ST25TB).
items.prov: Upstream; byte-identical base.

items.label: emv
items.desc: Reads EMV bank cards — AIP parse, SFI brute-force, PAN & cardholder extraction.
items.prov: U-origin, built incrementally (AIP, SFI brute, PAN/cardholder). R/M inherit byte-identical.

items.label: ntag4xx
items.desc: NTAG 4xx (ISO type-4) tag protocol support.
items.prov: U-origin (`fa6839d28` "nfc lib"); R/M byte-identical.

items.label: type_4_tag
items.desc: ISO type-4 tag read plus a card-emulation listener.
items.prov: U-origin (`fa6839d28`); R/M byte-identical.

items.label: MfUltralight-C 3DES key-page write
items.desc: Permits writing the Ultralight-C 3DES key page — the 'magic emulation key-grab'.
items.prov: U-origin; `mf_ultralight_listener.c:204-218` — "MAGIC: allow write to ULC key page". U=R=M md5 `9fbc7f41…`, differs from O.

items.label: Mfkey32 nonce capture
items.desc: Logs reader nonces ('Detect Reader') for offline MIFARE key cracking.
items.prov: Upstream OFW (`mfkey32_logger.c`).

items.label: On-device mfkey app (in tree)
items.desc: On-device MIFARE Classic key-recovery app vendored in the firmware tree.
items.prov: noproto/FlipperMfkey. Official ships it via App Hub (not in tree). U has it as a system app; R/M external. U=R `mfkey.c` md5-identical; crypto1 core byte-identical across all three.

items.label: Mfkey attack coverage
items.desc: Which key-recovery attacks the on-device app implements.
items.prov: mfkey32 + static-nested only. No hardnested / darkside (those stay PC-class).

items.label: MIFARE Classic key dictionary
items.desc: Plaintext dictionary of MIFARE keys for dictionary attacks; sizes diverge sharply.
items.prov: Plaintext key list. **Unleashed is ~2× the rest (4082 keys)**. R == M are **byte-identical key sets** (2475, same order; only comment case differs) — a shared-origin signal.

items.label: Ultralight-C key dictionary
items.desc: 3DES key dictionary for Ultralight-C; forks add two keys.
items.prov: Forks +2 keys; minor.

items.label: Magic-card writing (nfc_magic)
items.desc: Write/clone to magic cards; only RogueMaster and Momentum vendor the app.
items.prov: R/M vendor the full app; `gen4_poller.c` byte-identical R=M (`0d77609f…`). O ships via App Hub; U doesn't vendor it.

items.label: Magic types supported
items.desc: Magic-card generations the writer covers.
items.prov: Gen1A/B, Gen2, Gen4 GTU (incl. Ultralight/NTAG cloning via Gen4). Shared upstream nfc_magic.

items.label: Shared +14 transit/payment/lock parsers
items.desc: Fourteen card parsers (Charliecard, Metromoney, Saflok, Ventra, Zolotaya Korona…) added by Unleashed.
items.prov: U-origin; 12 of 14 byte-identical across U/R/M.

items.label: smartrider.c variant
items.desc: SmartRider (Perth) transit parser — Momentum carries a reformatted variant.
items.prov: M reformat/edit; M md5 differs from U=R.

items.label: ventra.c variant
items.desc: Ventra (Chicago) transit parser; RogueMaster adds a CTA station database.
items.prov: R adds a CTA station DB ("FatherDivine"); R md5 differs from U=M.

items.label: andalucia
items.desc: Consorcio Andalucía (Spain) transit-card parser; hardcoded key, sector 9.
items.prov: **RogueMaster-only.**

items.label: trea
items.desc: TREA (Italy) transit-card parser — RM-only and undocumented.
items.prov: **RogueMaster-only**, undocumented (`0252da598`).

items.label: hotels
items.desc: Saflok / VingCard / Onity hotel-lock parser; parse-only stub, dead on live read.
items.prov: **RogueMaster-only**, undocumented; verify/read are stubs (parse-only, dead on live read).

items.label: Hotel-lock parsing (saflok)
items.desc: Saflok hotel-door MIFARE lock parser — the closest 'key/lock' addition.
items.prov: Hotel-door MFC, not automotive.

items.label: Automotive digital-key NFC parser
items.desc: No car digital-key NFC parser exists in any fork — exhaustively confirmed.
items.prov: **None in any fork.** Every apparent "car key" match was a false positive — transit "Vehicle id", FeliCa `FelicaCardKey`, wav audio assets, unit-test fixtures.

items.label: External apps vendored in tree
items.desc: Count of external .fap apps shipped inside the firmware git tree.
items.prov: O/U distribute via catalogs (App Hub / all-the-plugins); **RogueMaster ships the largest in-tree pack (665)**.

items.label: nfc_magic
items.desc: Magic-card writer app — RogueMaster and Momentum vendor it.
items.prov: R/M vendor; shared upstream.

items.label: mfkey
items.desc: MIFARE key-recovery app (shared noproto upstream).
items.prov: U as system app; R/M external.

items.label: NFC Fuzzer / Sniffer / Relay / Dict Mgr
items.desc: RogueMaster-only NFC attack suite, including a live relay (MITM).
items.prov: **RogueMaster-only** in-tree; broadest NFC attack surface (Relay = live man-in-the-middle).

items.label: ProtoPirate
items.desc: Momentum car / rolling-code SubGhz app (AUT64, Chrysler, Ford, Honda… + relocated RU car alarms).
items.prov: **Momentum-bundled** external app; houses the relocated star_line/scher_khan/kia plus aut64/chrysler/ford/honda/… decoders. Not in U/R/O current trees.

items.label: ULC apps (brute / fkey / relay)
items.desc: Ultralight-C brute-force, key and relay tools.
items.prov: Shared @noproto; RogueMaster has a subset (brute + fkey), Momentum has all three.

items.label: weather_station / tpms / pocsag apps
items.desc: External sensor & pager apps (RogueMaster + Momentum bundle them).
items.prov: Community apps; Momentum also integrates them into the core lib.

items.label: Telemetry / phone-home
items.desc: Any analytics or beacon in the core firmware. None found — clean across all forks.
items.prov: No telemetry/phone-home in any fork-delta core firmware. Every `http(s)://` hit was a documentation/datasheet reference comment; no raw IPs, no beacons.

items.label: Covert exfil of captured secrets
items.desc: The crown-jewel question: does anything emit captured keys/dumps over radio/BLE/UART without user action? No.
items.prov: **No such path in any fork.** mfkey / NFC / SubGhz results stay local on SD. No auto-emission of captured material. (High confidence — fork-deltas were swept directly.)

items.label: Obfuscated / encoded payloads
items.desc: Hidden encoded blobs in source. Only standard base64 alphabet + legitimate crypto xor.
items.prov: No obfuscated payloads. base64/xor hits were the standard alphabet (find_my) and legit Crypto1 / Nice FloR-S rolling-code math.

items.label: Time bombs / date-gated logic
items.desc: Date- or time-triggered hidden behavior. None — all RTC code is legitimate.
items.prov: No date-triggered logic. All RTC/date code is clock UI, RPC datetime, and transit-card parsing.

items.label: Hardcoded sensitive keys (Keeloq)
items.desc: Larger Keeloq keystore — but AES-encrypted, no plaintext leaked.
items.prov: Forks ship a larger keystore (62→116 records) but it is **AES-encrypted**; the key is in the device enclave, not the repo. No plaintext keys leaked. See Keeloq keystore feature.

items.label: Hardcoded 3rd-party API key
items.desc: Momentum's stock-ticker toy app ships the developer's own AlphaVantage key (low).
items.prov: `flip_trader_callback.c:84` embeds `apikey=2X90WLEFMP43OJKE` — a leak of the **developer's own** credential, not any user secret. Severity: low (F-MOM-SEC-01).
evi: dev's own AlphaVantage key — not user data

items.label: BLE-HID pairing-PIN suppression
items.desc: BadBT auto-confirms the BLE pairing PIN — scoped to the user-launched attack tool.
items.prov: `suppress_pin_screen` makes `bt.c:95/112` skip the Verify-code dialog and auto-accept pairing. Set only by BadUSB BLE-HID mode (`bad_usb_hid.c:165/196`); flag is global for that window. Weakens pairing MITM-confirmation but is a deliberate, user-launched feature — not covert. Low.

items.label: RPC-while-locked toggle
items.desc: Momentum opt-in to allow RPC access while the device is locked (default OFF).
items.prov: Momentum-only opt-in (`rpc.c:389-392`), default OFF (F-MOM-SEC-02). Official blocks unconditionally; U/R audits found no locked-RPC toggle.

items.label: External network apps (ESP32/WiFi)
items.desc: Opt-in WiFi apps that send user-authored data — not captured secrets, not fork-unique.
items.prov: User-triggered ESP32/WiFi packs (JBlanked). Endpoints are app self-update/store + host-side AirTag tooling (user's own iCloud). No captures exfiltrated.
